newsitem.title: UK: OVERNIGHT-EUROSTOCKS SHRUG OFF EU PACT,END WITH LOSSES.
newsitem.headline: OVERNIGHT-EUROSTOCKS SHRUG OFF EU PACT,END WITH LOSSES.

text.p: European stocks ended trade with losses on Monday, unimpressed by EU leaders agreeing on a budget stability pact and discouraged by a poor early trade on Wall Street.

In currency markets, the dollar finished the session slightly down on the mark after profit-taking. Dealers said sentiment remained healthy as improved prospects for launching a single European currency would result in a soft euro, making "safe haven" currencies like the dollar an attractive investment.

Paris saw the most volatile trading. Stocks finished down about 0.5 percent despite the compromise agreement struck by EU leaders to enforce budget discipline in the single European currency zone and to create more jobs.
The blue chip CAC-40 index hit a record high of 2,825.18 points early in the day on on a wave of optimism that a deal would be reached at the summit meeting in Amsterdam.
But the mood changed later and stocks went into reverse. Even after the budget stability pact was announced, the market failed to perk up and slipped well into the red by the close.

French investors ignored the news from Amsterdam where the ministers resolved the differences between France and other member countries over jobs, and concentrated on the bad news from New York where the Dow Jones made an negative start after a six-day record-breaking run last week .

London had a rough day. The FTSE 100, after Friday's record close, finished the day down 0.8 percent, unsettled by Wall Street and press reports of an attack on tax breaks for pension funds in the next budget. The FTSE 100 index set three

closing records last week but the bullish mood was dented by the talk that dividend tax benefits might be axed in the July 2 budget in a move that would target the corporate sector rather than cooling consumer spending
"It's all down to the news on the government's tax-raising plans," said one trader. "There's definitely been a shift in sentiment."
The one bright spot was insurer Norwich Union's market debut. The shares rose to 356p in early trade compared with a public offer price of 290p. But by the close the shares had slipped to 324-1/2p.

In Frankfurt, floor trading, which ended before Wall Street began, closed with healthy gains but dealings on the computerised IBIS index fell because of the poor start on Wall Street and the weaker dollar.
The DAX-30 index put on over 0.5 percent close at 3,765.11 points but volume was weak.

In currencies, the dollar was slightly down against the mark and yen in late dealings as the market digested the EMU agreement on budget stability and looked ahead to this week's G7 summit meeting of leading industrial countries. The dollar

strengthened initially against the mark as news broke of the stability pact. The deal was seen as helping the dollar but the U.S. currency received only little lift as the outcome was already largely factored into exchange rates.
The gains were eroded by profit-taking. "There was no surprise out of the stability pact and some profit-takers have come out," said a U.S. bank dealer. " The dollar was trading
at 1.7295 marks in late Europe and, against the Japanese currency, was down over a yen at 113.55 compared to late Friday's level of 114.73.
The drop against the yen came as last week's worries lingered about U.S.-Japanese trade friction ahead of a Group of Seven (G7) summit in Denver on June 20.

The market fears that the trade imbalance could prompt a clash between the U.S. and Japan, although an international monetary source helped calm those concerns by saying G7 leaders might not single out Japan's surplus for attention.
Focus has now turned to this week's Japanese and U.S. trade data which will be more acutely felt as they come just before the G7 summit. CURRENCIES AT 1600 GMT The dollar was at
1.7295 marks and 113.55 yen, compared with 1.7373 and 114.73 in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index finished down 38.0 points at 4,745.1
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed down 12.65 points at 2795.87.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended up 20.67 at 3,765.11.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at 341.75 an ounce, compared with Friday's close of 341.55. Silver was down one cent at 4.72 in late trade.
